speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any cognitive changes, memory loss, or personality shifts alongside your balance issues? Also, have you had any family members diagnosed with similar neurological conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a crucial piece of information; natalizumab is used for Multiple Sclerosis, but could it be affecting your spinal cord? Given your history of Crohn's disease and current medication, have you experienced any new numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs recently?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine with contrast.
REQUEST TEST: Antibody panel for anti-MOG and anti-AQP4.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced myelitis or Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.
